info.title: Nex Core pool peer API
info.description: Internal Core-to-Core pool peer contract; not a client or Controller API. Nex Controller never calls it and holds none of its state: membership, the pool CA, repository reservations, pool VM execution records and clustered-storage operations are durable on the pool master Core (peer probe leases and access observations are process-local). Served on the dedicated peer HTTPS listener (--pool-peer-listen, default :9444, on nex-core-local and nex-core-agent), TLS 1.3 only, with server limits of 5 s header, 15 s read, 30 s write and 16 KiB headers. The listener requests a client certificate and verifies it against the pool CA when presented; every route except join then admits only the peer named by its security requirement. Clients pin the pool CA and expected host ID (and, master to member, the membership certificate SHA-256), refuse redirects and time out after 15 s. Errors are short text/plain bodies. Development protocol: deploy matching Core versions in a pool; additive acknowledgements (probe mode echo, update_accepted, spec_match) let newer peers fail closed against older ones.

servers.description: Pool peer listener of a Core host; never the Controller or host-local API origin.

post.summary: Redeem a pool join offer
post.description: Served by the pool master; the only peer route without a client certificate. Authority is the single-use offer created by the master Core local API: it binds pool, master host, member host ID and CSR SHA-256, and expires after 15 minutes. The master signs the CSR with the pool CA, appends the member as ready, increments the membership generation and persists before replying. A retry of the same offer, host ID and CSR after a lost response returns the same certificate and current membership; a different key or an already-admitted host is refused. The member pins the pool CA and master host ID from the offer, verifies the returned certificate against its pending key, then persists and completes a Core-owned rehome. Body at most 1 MiB.
post.x-audience: Core peer: joining host → pool master

post.summary: Advertise member peer origin, system UUID, management-controller report and watchdog
post.description: Served by the pool master. Records the calling member's peer listener origin, its own SMBIOS system UUID, its own management-controller report and its own watchdog capability in the master membership: the origin so the master can later contact that member (PoolMasterCertificate routes), the UUID so another host can prove a management controller belongs to this machine before fencing it, and the watchdog so the master can answer whether that host could shut itself out after it is gone. Each field is recorded on its own and either may be omitted; both are observations and move no membership generation. The member is identified only by its certificate; input cannot name another member. Last write wins and repeats are idempotent; an unknown member is accepted without change. The member persists a pending origin first and retries it at startup until the master returns 204. Body at most 4 KiB; any non-POST method is rejected as 400 after authentication.

post.summary: Check one member's native VM placement
post.description: Served by the current ready selected member at its advertised origin and called only by its current pool master over pinned mutual TLS. The request names one exact vm-create or vm-update command and the current membership generation. The member reads its current durable managed state, including the no-effect clustered-storage admission context, and performs no mutation, reservation, or start. It returns only after native placement checks complete and after rechecking membership. The master accepts an acknowledgement only when generation, operation_id, vm_id and vm echo exactly and accepted is true; before saving its definition or reservation it takes its durable locks and rechecks that same membership generation. A missing acknowledgement field from an older Core, timeout, connection failure, refusal or membership change fails placement closed. replay:true means the target recognized the identical existing journal command and did no fresh native check; it may confirm only an existing durable master placement record, never create one. A failed placement admission for an exact journalled definition command does not authorize native execution or journal reconciliation; Core reports needs_attention. Retry only the same operation and command after reconciliation; changed input with the same operation is refused. Requests and master-accepted replies are bounded to 128 KiB; the member's preflight deadline is 20 seconds.

get.summary: Report what authority replica this member holds
get.description: Served by a pool member at its advertised peer origin and called only by its current pool master over pinned mutual TLS. Read-only. It is also how the master learns the member's certified peer public key for the per-member key wrap, from the pinned TLS leaf of this call, so no public key is ever put on the wire or into the membership record. An empty object is returned when this host holds no replica. Answering also refreshes the member's own observation window, so a member the master is polling does not report its replica as stale.

post.summary: Store one signed authority replica on this member
post.description: Master to member over pinned mutual TLS, bounded to 1 MiB with no trailing JSON. The member verifies that the replica names its own pool and its current master, is addressed to itself, declares every section with matching digests, and is signed by the pool CA it pinned at join; it then writes pool-replica.json atomically at mode 0600 and acknowledges. It never acts on the contents: no membership, VM, storage, network or media record on this host is read from or changed by a replica, a replica grants no execution, and no health judgement is derived from one. Idempotent: the same generation with the same content returns the same acknowledgement. A strictly lower generation is refused, and the same generation with different content is refused rather than overwriting. The wrapped pool CA key is stored sealed and is not opened by anything in this release. Pushes are driven by the master's probe tick when its authority content digest has changed or a member is behind, so a member may lag by up to one probe interval; nothing waits on a replica.

post.summary: Hold a cross-Core probe lock lease
post.description: Served by the pool master. Takes a non-blocking OFD write lock on one byte of .nex-peer-lock in the repository path so the member can prove it observes the same shared filesystem (it must see a conflict, then acquire after DELETE). challenge-byte-v1 uses a nonzero offset derived from SHA-256 of the challenge and echoes X-Nex-Pool-Probe-Mode; absent probe_mode uses legacy byte zero. The lease is bound to caller, repository, generation, challenge and mode; replaying the same held lease returns 204. Leases expire after ten seconds, at most 64 are active, and they are not VM ownership or fencing authority.

post.summary: Admit a pool VM execution transition
post.description: Served by the pool master, serialized per master. The owner member asks the master to durably record a VM definition or execution transition before acting locally; the master writes its record before replying. For define(create=true) and update-reserve, before taking the durable VM lock the master obtains the selected current member's exact authenticated native placement preflight; no lock spans that RPC. It validates returned shared-storage observations and persists the definition or exact next revision before setting placement_accepted=true. Actions: define (create=true seeds a new record from a valid vm owned by the caller; otherwise spec_match reports whether vm matches the durable definition), start (defined/stopped → starting, epoch+1, returns a random permit), running (starting → running), stop (owner check only), stopped (owner proves stop; placement retained), reboot (requires running) and media (owner check only), update-reserve (reserve one exact next revision), update-commit and update-abort (settle it with exact local journal evidence). Only the recorded owner may transition a VM; there is no expiry or timeout cleanup, so unknown execution stays fenced and an unreachable host is never treated as stopped. Retries after a lost reply reconcile the exact durable definition or reservation; a missing placement_accepted acknowledgement, preflight timeout or membership change fails closed. Body at most 1 MiB.

post.summary: Perform one step of a pool master change or eject on this host

Every action is idempotent by operation_id: the same request repeated after a lost reply returns the same answer and performs the step at most once. An activation is taken only against a replica this host already holds and has verified at exactly the generation the outgoing master froze and signed away; nothing here recomputes or invents authority. A re-point is adopted only from a signed notice whose membership generation is strictly higher than this host's.

Admitted to any holder of a certificate this pool's CA issued, including one this pool has ejected: an ejected host must be able to learn that it is no longer a member, and it can only learn that from the pool that ejected it. The caller's own membership status is decided from the certificate the transport proved, never from a name in a body. A pool master answering a ready member that is behind also returns a pool-CA-signed re-point notice, so a host that missed a push converges from whichever host it can reach without having to trust a stale one; the probe answer alone changes nothing, only the signature at a strictly higher generation does. Optional query ?vms=1 adds this host's own view of the VM definitions it owns, which the promotion proof of a later slice consumes. The handler also accepts POST with an identical, equally read-only answer, so a caller behind a transport that dislikes one method can use the other; nothing in Nex Core calls the POST form, so it is described here rather than documented as a separate operation.

parameters.description: Ask for this host's own VM ownership records.

200.description: This host's own authority, membership and transfer state.

401.description: "pool peer certificate is required".

405.description: Method other than GET or POST; Allow: GET, POST.

409.description: "pool membership is unavailable".

post.summary: Report what this host found on the other hosts' fence devices
post.description: Served by the pool master. Every ready host periodically reads every other host's management controller over the recorded fence profile and the replicated credential, asking which machine it manages and reading that machine's power state, and sends the results here. The read is non-destructive by construction: no power-off is reachable from that code path. The member certificate says which host is calling and the whole report is credited to that host; a claim it makes about its own row is dropped, because a host does not get to say whether it can be shut out. The master keeps these in memory, overlays them on the membership it reports and never writes them into its durable membership record, so a pool's signed authority does not move because a check ran; a master that restarts reports "not checked yet" until the next pass. Safe to repeat: a later report replaces the caller's previous one. Body at most 64 KiB.

204.description: The report was recorded against the calling host.

400.description: Invalid JSON, a body over 64 KiB, more than 64 results, an unsupported result or an invalid detail.

401.description: Missing or unverified client certificate, or the caller is not an admitted ready member of this pool.

405.description: Method not allowed (sent after authentication); `Allow: POST`.

409.description: This host is not the pool master, so it keeps no fence checks.

post.summary: Offer the pool master the fence device this host configured on its own controller
post.description: Served by the pool master. The member certificate says which host is calling and the profile is recorded for that host only: a member cannot offer a fence device for another host. The master writes the password into its own private fence-credential store first, because the identity check that follows signs in with it, and then records the profile through exactly the path an operator-entered profile takes — including proving over the network that the controller really manages that host's machine, and refusing to replace a profile an operator entered by hand. Nothing is recorded if any step refuses, and the refusal sentence is returned so the member can report it. Idempotent in effect: a member that has already had its profile recorded does not call this again, and a repeat records the same profile with fresh material. Body at most 8 KiB.

204.description: The profile and its material were recorded in the master's membership.

400.description: Invalid JSON or a body over 8 KiB.

401.description: Missing or unverified client certificate, or the caller is not an admitted ready member of this pool.

405.description: Method not allowed (sent after authentication); `Allow: POST`.

409.description: The master refused, in its own sentence: "this is not a fence device a host configured for itself", "this pool master could not keep the fence account's password", "this host already has a fence device an operator set, so the one it configured for itself was not recorded", "only the pool master records a fence profile", "no such member of this pool", or any refusal of the identity proof such as "the management controller at this address reports a different machine than the host it is recorded for; nothing was powered off".

PoolMemberCertificate.description: Served only by the pool master (this Core holds the pool CA key and is the membership master). The client certificate must chain to the pool CA, its subject CN must be a membership host ID whose status is ready, and its SHA-256 must equal that member's recorded certificate_sha256.

PoolMasterCertificate.description: Served only by a pool member (not the master). The client certificate must chain to the pool CA, its subject CN must be the membership master host ID with ready status, and its SHA-256 must equal the master's recorded certificate_sha256.

PoolPeerCertificate.description: Served by any pool host. The client certificate must chain to this host's pool CA. What it admits then depends on the route and the action: the read-only authority probe admits any holder of a certificate this pool's CA issued, including one this pool has ejected, and reports the caller's own membership status back rather than refusing it; a transfer activate, abort or leave admits only this host's current pinned pool master; a transfer repoint admits any host whose certificate matches a ready membership row, because the sender has just become the pool master and this host does not know that yet.

ClusterMemberStatus.description: Member clustered-storage report. updated_at is replaced by the master clock on receipt.

ISCSIStorageSource.description: exclusive is the legacy single-writer profile and needs exclusive_target. clustered_gfs2 instead requires cluster_id, lock_table and three to five unique eligible hosts, rejects exclusive_target, and only accepts an existing GFS2 filesystem; Core never formats it.

filesystem_id.description: New Core-observed identities use the NFSv4 kernel protocol FSID profile nfs4:<mounted-server-address-hex>:<port-hex>:<fsid-major-hex>:<fsid-minor-hex>. Core binds that profile to stat.Dev and one matching /proc/fs/nfsfs/volumes row, then verifies the requested source. Missing or ambiguous rows fail closed; a zero protocol FSID is valid. Address changes fail closed and are not NFS HA failover. Preserved legacy statfs identities remain representable, are not auto-upgraded, and fail closed.

directory.description: Validated existing relative subdirectory beneath the original NFS export; spaces are supported, traversal, backslashes and control characters are rejected.

origin.description: Bare https:// origin: no user info, path, query or fragment. It may be omitted or empty when system_uuid is sent on its own.

system_uuid.description: This member's own SMBIOS system UUID, in any usual spelling; the master normalizes it to 32 lower-case hex digits and refuses known firmware placeholders (all-zero, all-ff and the common 03000200-0400-0500-0006-000700080009). Recorded in the member's membership row and used to prove a management controller belongs to this machine before a fence powers it off. The master records it only in the calling member's own row, and refuses two changes that would let a host defeat its own fencing: replacing an identity it already reported while a BMC fence profile is recorded against it (clearing the profile is the motherboard-replacement path), and claiming an identity another member of the pool already holds. A refused value is dropped silently — the request still returns 204 when the origin was recorded — and the member simply cannot be given a BMC fence device. Members send it at join and on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining; a member too old to send one is unaffected.

bmc.description: What this member's own Nex Core found and did about its own management controller. Recorded in the calling member's own row; the state must be one of the closed set and the sentence is bounded at 1 KiB, or the request is refused with 400. It is an observation and nothing more: a host cannot change what the pool decided about it, so a report of state "removed" does not delete the fence device the pool recorded — withdrawing one is an operator decision authenticated at the Controller and recorded by the master. A report that does not differ from the one already recorded, except in its timestamp, is not written at all, so a settled pool's signed authority does not move because a host keeps saying the same thing. Like the other two fields it may be sent on its own and it moves no membership generation.

watchdog.description: The watchdog device this member's own Nex Core found on the machine it runs on, read from sysfs without ever opening the device node. Recorded in the calling member's own row; the kind must be one of the closed set and the strings are bounded, or the request is refused with 400. Like the other fields it is an observation, it may be sent on its own, it moves no membership generation, and a report that does not differ from the one already recorded is not written at all, so a settled pool's signed authority does not move because a host keeps saying the same thing. Members send it on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining; a member too old to send one leaves the field absent, which never counts as a watchdog.

watchdog_armed.description: This member's own report that it has armed the watchdog above, recorded in the calling member's own row. It is the first of the three conditions of a watchdog exclusion proof, so unlike the capability beside it the master keeps it durably and replicates it: the host that has to read it is a promotion candidate whose master has gone. Refused with 400 if the kind is not one a watchdog exclusion could rest on, or the strings are unbounded. A report that does not differ from the one already recorded is not written at all, so a settled pool's signed authority does not move because a reconcile pass ran. A member too old to send one leaves the field absent, which never counts.

PeerAdvertiseRequest.description: What a member advertises about itself: where it listens, which machine it is, what its own Core found on its management controller, and the watchdog that machine has. Each field is recorded on its own and any of them may be omitted.

PeerJoinRequest.description: Untagged Go struct: JSON members use Go field names (case-insensitive on decode). Offer is the raw offer token, not the encoded offer.

CSRPEM.description: PEM certificate request whose subject CN equals HostID and whose SHA-256 matches the offer.

PeerJoinResponse.description: Signed member certificate (TLS client and server auth, two-year validity) and the master membership after admission.

observed_at.description: When the master admitted this member, or created the pool for its founding host. Nothing rewrites it afterwards; the Controller reports it as joined_at.

peer_origin.description: Bare HTTPS origin this member advertised to the master for peer traffic. Recorded from the member's own advertisement, or, for the master's own row, from the master_url of the first Controller-driven join, which the master works out itself when none is supplied; never inferred from Controller connectivity.

system_uuid.description: This host's own SMBIOS system UUID, 32 lower-case hex digits without separators, reported by the host itself while it was alive: at join, and on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining. It is what proves a management controller belongs to this machine before it is powered off. Like peer_origin it is a recorded observation and moves no generation. A host too old to report one stays empty and simply cannot be given a BMC fence device.

replica_generation.description: The master's observation of the authority-replica generation this member last acknowledged. Memory-only on the master and overlaid on the reported copy of the membership record: it is never written into the durable membership and is never an input to the generation equality rule. A member that has never acknowledged one is reported at 0, honestly.

replica_digest.description: Content digest the member acknowledged, as observed by the master.

replica_error.description: The master's bounded reason for the last failed push to this member: "pool member does not support pool-authority-replica-v1; upgrade it before relying on its replica", "pool member did not report its authority replica", "pool member did not acknowledge the authority replica", "pool member refused the authority replica" or the member's own refusal text, "pool authority replica exceeds the peer body limit", or "pool member peer certificate cannot receive a wrapped pool CA key".

replica_observed_at.description: When the master made that observation. Zero when it has none.

fence.description: How this host would be excluded from the pool if it had to be fenced: the same closed typed profile clustered storage already uses, recorded in the master's durable membership and replicated with it, so a promoted master inherits it and a fresh Controller re-adopts it. Only a virsh profile can be recorded by this build; Core refuses to record a profile it cannot verify. The credential reference it carries is never projected to a client, and neither is anything the reference names.

fence_credential_version.description: The master's counter for the private fence credential material behind this host's profile. The material itself is never in the membership; only this number is, so rotating it changes the replicated content and therefore advances the pool authority generation, while re-recording identical material moves nothing.

fence_readiness.description: The pool master's own answer to whether this host could be shut out, per method. Reported only by the master, only for the membership it owns, and never written into the durable record. Absent from a Core too old to report it, which a Controller shows as "not reported" and never as ready.

system_uuid_conflict_host_id.description: The member that already reported the hardware identity this host reports, when the master refused this host's report because of it. Without it the refusal is a dead end: an operator is told their host has no unique identity with nothing to act on. Cleared the moment the identity is accepted.

bmc.description: What this host's own Core found and did about its own management controller, reported to the master over the existing advertise peer route. It is an observation and a result, never a credential.

bmc_provisioning_disabled.description: The operator's own decision, recorded by the master, that this host must not configure its management controller for fencing. Clearing a fence device Nex Core provisioned sets it — one operator action with one meaning — and the host removes the account it created when it sees it. It is a decision, not an observation, so it lives with the fence profile in the replicated membership and a host cannot set or clear it by reporting about itself.

watchdog.description: This host's own watchdog capability, reported by the host and recorded by the master. A member too old to report one leaves it null, which is never counted.

watchdog_armed.description: That host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, recorded durably by the master. Null means the host never said, which is never a watchdog exclusion proof.

host_fencing_disabled.description: The pool's Host fencing setting, recorded the way it is decided: fencing is on for a pool that has never been told otherwise, so an absent field is on and a record written before the setting existed keeps the default. It is a decision, so it is durable, replicated and only ever written by the master.

fence_summary.description: The pool's fencing count, setting and prerequisite checklist, computed by the master over this membership when it reports it. Like the readiness on each member row it is a memory-only observation overlaid on the reported copy and never part of the durable record.

identity.description: Core-canonical secret-free identity observed after member preparation.

locking.description: Member proved the shared non-blocking lock against the master for this generation.

PoolStorageReservationRequest.description: Authenticated member-to-master peer request. The master binds the reservation to the mTLS member identity, not a client host field.

PoolStorageTransfer.description: One master repository record addressed to the calling member: storage.host_id is rewritten to the caller and member_access is cleared. credentials is present only for SMB repositories and carries the secret over peer mTLS; the member stores it only in its own Core credential state.

deleted.description: VM IDs this member durably deleted: succeeded vm-delete tombstones from its own managed journal. Positive evidence of removal, which is what lets the master prune its pool-vms.json owner record for a VM; absence is never read as deletion.

PoolVMInventory.description: Complete, membership-generation-bound VM inventory of the reporting member. updates carries only exact successful local managed-journal evidence for a current revision; deleted carries this member's own delete tombstones.

command.description: The supported subset of Command; operation_id must equal the enclosing operation_id and vm must be non-null.

PoolPlacementRequest.description: The exact managed vm-create or vm-update command that the master is about to admit; command.operation_id must equal operation_id.

error.description: Sanitized refusal reason, emitted only with HTTP 409; CR, LF and NUL are replaced by a generic reason.

PoolPlacementReply.description: A read-only target-host observation. On 200, vm is an exact echo of the requested definition and accepted is true only when all native preflight checks passed. replay is present only when an identical existing target journal command was recognized; it cannot authorize a new master record. On 409, only error is emitted. The master must reject a missing, changed or false acknowledgement.

PoolVMRequest.description: Request and response share this shape: the master echoes the request after setting epoch and, per action, permit, spec_match, update_accepted, update_revision and placement_accepted. placement_accepted is true only after the master has received a fresh exact target-host preflight and durably recorded the create definition or update reservation. Older masters omit acknowledgement fields; clients must treat a missing acknowledgement as unsafe.

filesystem_id.description: Diagnostic CIFS filesystem ID; it is not durable across reconnects.

marker_id.description: Core-created atomic durable share-root marker for new registrations. Core verifies it with the exact SMB source/options after reconnect. Absent only on preserved legacy records, which retain strict filesystem-ID failure behavior and are not auto-upgraded.

share.description: Ordinary share name: letters, numbers, internal spaces and ._$:()-; no leading/trailing whitespace or path/command/unit syntax.

directory.description: Validated existing relative subdirectory below the SMB share, including spaces; never an SMB path. Traversal, backslashes and control characters are rejected.

shared.description: Core-observed shared-storage capability, never by itself permission to place or start a VM. Provisioned ZFS is always false because each selected host has an independent local zpool.

StorageClusterConfig.description: Core-owned clustered-GFS2 projection. Controller relay input never grants a caller-owned device path, mount path, proof, or secret; Core derives/verifies those native details.

username.description: Management-controller account for redfish and ipmilan, with power control only. It is not a secret and is reported back; its password is the credential. Absent on virsh and scsi_pr profiles, and a BMC profile without one can never produce a proof.

tls_fingerprint.description: Core captures the certificate the controller presents when the profile is recorded, keeps its leaf SHA-256 here and holds every later connection to exactly it: a factory management controller is self-signed with no usable name, so this pin, not a chain, identifies the endpoint the password is sent to and the power-off is issued through. A changed certificate refuses the fence with its own sentence rather than as a network fault. Reported so an operator can compare it with the controller's own page; it is not a secret and a client never supplies one. Absent on ipmilan, which authenticates its RMCP+ session and presents no certificate, and on virsh and scsi_pr.

virsh_uri.description: For virsh, exactly qemu:///system or qemu+ssh://<ssh_login>@<endpoint>[:<ssh_port>]/system. The latter must match the pinned SSH fields; it rejects passwords, query strings, fragments and every other URI path. An omitted URI port is valid only when ssh_port is 22.

cipher.description: The RMCP+ cipher suite an ipmilan fence must use, as the controller's own LAN channel offers it. Core selects it itself — 17 where the controller offers it, otherwise 3, the suite every IPMI 2.0 controller must implement — either while provisioning the account in-band or while proving a profile an operator entered. Suite 0 asks for no authentication, no integrity and no confidentiality, so it is never selected and never accepted here. Absent means none was recorded and ipmitool's own default is used. A client never supplies it; a request that does is refused with 400.

provisioned_by_core.description: The account behind this profile is one Nex Core created on the host's own management controller in-band. It is how a host knows, after a reboot or a master change, that the account under the Nex name is its own to replace rather than somebody else's to leave alone, and it is why an operator-entered profile is never overwritten by automatic provisioning. Written only by the pool master when the host's own Core reports the account it created; a client never supplies it, and a request that does is refused with 400.

StorageClusterFence.description: Closed Core fence profile. credential_ref and ssh_host_key_ref are opaque names for root-only Core secrets, never secret bytes; arbitrary commands and arguments are not accepted. Before any power-off Core asks the management controller which machine it manages — the Redfish ComputerSystem.UUID, compared exactly, or IPMI Get System GUID, where either documented byte order counts — and compares it with the target host's own SMBIOS system UUID in the master's membership record. A mismatch, a host with no unique hardware identity and an unreadable controller each refuse the fence and power nothing off. Redirects are never followed, so the identity cannot be read from one machine while another is powered off. A Redfish fence is performed by Core itself over the pinned connection — identity GET, ComputerSystem.Reset ForceOff, then a separate PowerState read — rather than by fence_redfish, which cannot be bound to the recorded certificate. virsh is for a Nex Core running as a virtual machine in a disposable lab and remains unaccepted for native production use.

request_id.description: Optional stable ID of the actual destructive fence attempt. A Core verifies this binding before accepting a peer receipt.

method.description: How the exclusion was proved. Absent is a fence device Nex Core powered the host off through and independently observed off, which is every proof there was before watchdog fencing. watchdog is the host resetting itself, whose evidence is the record beside it. A clustered-storage fence only ever produces the absent one.

watchdog.description: The evidence of a watchdog exclusion, present only when method says so.

StorageClusterFenceStatus.description: Core-recorded result of an actual fence/exclusion observation, bound to a request ID when destructive work was attempted and to an exact configuration generation and digest.

StorageClusterProjection.description: Private peer projection of one clustered-storage operation. auth_key is the pool corosync authkey; secrets are addressed only to the calling member. Must never cross the Controller boundary.

session_monitor_ready.description: Authenticated member attestation that the fixed local transport-monitor wrapper and CLI are installed and passed a successful live exact portal/IQN session probe. It is distinct from aggregate GFS2 or cluster health, and is projected to Controller only after storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 is acknowledged.

StorageCredentials.description: Transient credential bytes only. Optional domain is the SMB workgroup or AD domain used with username/secret. The selected operation validates the applicable secret form; inventory, journals, results and diagnostics never carry these fields.

spares.description: Hot spares. They are erased like the data disks, added as spare vdevs and the pool is created with autoreplace=on, so ZFS resilvers onto one by itself when a data disk fails. They satisfy no part of the layout rule.

ZFSReplaceRequest.description: Replace one failed leaf device of a provisioned ZFS repository's pool on one host. old_device names the leaf exactly as the pool observation reports it, and device is one candidate from POST /api/v1/storage/discover with kind zfs-device, carrying the same identity, fingerprint and typed erase confirmation rules the ZFS wizard uses. Core revalidates both against a fresh observation of the pool and the disk before it touches anything.

operation_id.description: Core operation identity. The executing host journals its replacement under it, so a redelivered command replays the recorded outcome instead of acting again.

host_id.description: The configured host whose pool holds the failed disk. It may be the pool master or a ready current member.

old_device.description: The failed leaf's /dev/disk/by-id path, as the repository's pool observation reports it.

ZFSProvisionHostResult.description: Durable outcome for one selected host. pool_guid and dataset_guid identify that host's independent native zpool and dataset after a successful provision; this outcome alone is not a current access observation.

ZFSHostAccess.description: Current per-host observation for a Core-provisioned local ZFS repository. The GUIDs, path, capacity and read/write flags apply only to host_id; a missing or errored observation grants no placement permission.

ZFSPoolStatus.description: Core's transient `zpool status` observation of one imported pool. Nothing durable is derived from it: the Controller passes it through and a fresh Controller sees it again on the next report.

ZFSPoolScan.description: A running or completed scrub or resilver. ZFS formats its own sizes and timestamps, so they are reported as the strings it produced.

parent.description: replacing or spare when this leaf sits under an in-flight replacement or activated-spare vdev; omitted for an ordinary data leaf.

ZFSPoolDevice.description: One leaf of the pool's vdev tree, named as the pool was created: the /dev/disk/by-id path for a Core-provisioned repository. parent marks an in-flight replacing or spare vdev.

zfs_host_access.description: Current local access observations for each configured host of a Core-provisioned ZFS repository.

zfs_provisioned.description: True only for a repository created through Core ZFS provisioning.

zfs_scope.description: Requested ZFS scope (host or pool). Pool scope shares the Core repository identity across independent host-local zpools; it does not make storage shared.

StorageRegistration.description: Core-owned repository configuration and observation. A repository has one selected host in this release; shared is a capability observation, never placement permission. Source identity, access, capacity and health are Core observations; a missing or replaced mount blocks writes and never falls back to a mountpoint. For existing-dataset ZFS registration, source.zfs.mount_path remains the existing dataset mount and path is the Core-owned /var/lib/nex-storage/<repository-id> bind alias used by VM disks; detach removes only that alias and never ZFS properties. Core ZFS provisioning creates its own tagged pool and vms dataset, then uses the same alias. Credentials remain Core-local and inventory reports only presence. A fresh Controller adopts these records from Inventory.managed.storage.

firmware.description: uefi is the default and requires EFI firmware advertised by the host's libvirt domain capabilities; bios stays selectable.

machine.description: Empty selects Core's default machine type (q35).

media_boot_order.description: 0 keeps the CD drive out of the boot order; any other value joins the disks' contiguous 1..N numbering. Every VM has the drive, so the order is kept while it is empty and an ISO can be ejected from a running guest.

secure_boot.description: UEFI Secure Boot. Omitted means on with the Microsoft keys enrolled, which is exactly what libvirt already selected for every UEFI VM defined before this field existed, so a definition re-sent unchanged keeps the firmware its guest was installed with. off selects the plain OVMF build with no enrolled keys, for unsigned boot media or drivers. Requires uefi; on with bios is rejected. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not offer a matching firmware build, naming the setting rather than passing libvirt's firmware-selection error through. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off.

tpm.description: Emulated TPM. 2.0 adds a tpm-crb device backed by swtpm; omitted and none add no device, so a definition written before this field keeps exactly the devices it had. Windows 11 requires a TPM and refuses to install without one. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not advertise the emulator backend, rather than defining a device that cannot start. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off, and REMOVING a TPM is refused outright at any time: anything the guest sealed to it, including a Windows BitLocker key, would be lost, and libvirt cleans TPM state by iterating the devices the persistent definition still carries, so a redefine without it would orphan that state.

VMBoot.description: Firmware, Secure Boot, TPM, machine type and the install media's place in the boot order. Boot order is per device (libvirt forbids mixing per-device boot with an os/boot device list), so at least one disk or the install media must carry a non-zero order.

count.description: vCPUs presented to the guest. Both sides require at least 1; Controller caps the request at 64 and refuses more than the host reports.

sockets.description: Sockets, or 0 with cores and threads for the default topology.

cores.description: Cores per socket, or 0 for the default topology.

threads.description: Threads per core, or 0 for the default topology.

model.description: Host modes follow the current host; named models come from native host capabilities. New wizard drafts choose the current pool CPU baseline when available, storing its exact model/features. Explicit feature-bearing definitions are compared against the actual VM machine and runtime. Baseline compatibility covers current members only, not future hosts or live migration. CPU choices are independent of guest OS.

features.description: Optional fixed native CPU feature list. Omitted or empty retains model-only behavior. Nonempty requires a named model (not host modes or max) and vm-cpu-baseline-v1. Duplicate feature names are rejected.

VMCPU.description: vCPU count, optional topology and CPU model. Sockets, cores and threads all 0 select the default topology of one socket, count cores and one thread; otherwise each must be at least 1 and sockets × cores × threads must equal count. JSON Schema cannot express that product, so Controller and Core both enforce it in protocol.ValidateVMSpec.

id.description: Controller-assigned stable UUID; identity is preserved across Controller replacement and later migration.

name.description: Nonblank VM name, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (the byte limit is additionally enforced by Controller and Core). Spaces, case, dots, punctuation and Unicode are preserved exactly. Slashes, control characters and XML-invalid U+FFFE/U+FFFF are rejected. Core checks uniqueness on the host, journals the name and reports it for Controller adoption; failed or uncertain creations retain their reservation. Upgrade Controller and Core together to use the expanded naming syntax.

description.description: Free-text operator note, at most 4096 characters.

guest_os.description: Guest OS hint recorded for display and guest-tools advice; empty leaves it unset. It installs nothing and does not change the VM devices: disk bus and NIC model are chosen per device.

disks.description: One to eight disks; names unique within the VM.

media_id.description: Install ISO (Media.id), empty for none. The ISO must be imported and verified on the placement host; it may live on any storage that host can read and does not need to share a repository with the VM's disks. Every VM has the CD drive, so a non-zero boot.media_boot_order does not require media_id: an emptied drive keeps its place in the boot order.

drivers_media_id.description: ISO in the VM's second CD drive, for a driver disc an installer needs alongside its install media - a Windows guest installing to a VirtIO disk needs the virtio-win ISO here. Empty leaves that drive empty; the drive itself always exists on a host reporting vm-media-drivers-drive-v1. Must differ from media_id.

start_after_create.description: Honoured by the host inside the creation, after the definition is verified, so the creation itself has succeeded whether or not the flag is set: Core starts the guest exactly once and records the outcome in the journal entry's start field. A failed automatic start leaves the VM defined and stopped as a normal managed VM (power, console and media work; a replacement Controller adopts it) and is reported by the host as its own outcome with ID <operation-id>:start, kind vm-power, status failed and error 'VM created but not started: <reason>', which Controller records in Task history. A creation interrupted at the start step reconciles by observing libvirt: running means started, otherwise that outcome reads 'interrupted before the automatic start completed'. A failed or uncertain creation never boots. Controller issues no follow-on power request. Must be false in an edit.

autostart.description: libvirt autostart, set while the stopped guest is defined so the host starts this VM on boot. It is not a start.

tags.description: Operator labels kept with the VM definition: each 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, at most 16. Controller sorts and de-duplicates them before validation; an invalid tag is 400 naming it (tag "<tag>" must be 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens), more than 16 distinct tags is 400 (a VM allows at most 16 tags). Tags are part of the complete definition, so an edit that omits them clears them. Nonempty tags need vm-tags-v1 on both the VM's host and its pool master, because an older Core would drop them: 409 "the VM's host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core" on updateVM and "the selected host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core" on createVM, after the replay check. Core journals them with the definition, the pool master keeps them in its pool VM record, and a fresh Controller adopts them from the host's reported definition. Omitted when empty and from older Core. They change no guest device and apply to a running VM. Introduced in development product 0.4.8.

revision.description: Definition revision: 0 at creation, current + 1 for each edit. Core refuses any other value, so a stale edit after Controller replacement fails instead of applying an old definition. Reported back in Inventory.managed.vms with the current definition.

VMCreateSpec.description: The complete VM specification: Controller-assigned UUID and pool membership with separate host assignment, identity, CPU, memory, every disk and network interface, boot and install media, and the two lifecycle switches. Creation defines a stopped VM and never boots it. Dependencies must have succeeded on this host and pool. Both sides validate the shared bounds through protocol.ValidateVMSpec; Controller owns identity, reference existence, pool-wide MAC uniqueness and capacity.

storage_id.description: Registered storage that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool. Core resolves it by resource ID, not by pool/host ID, so it survives Controller replacement.

name.description: Operator-facing disk name, unique within the VM. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, starting with a letter or digit; it is not a path.

bus.description: virtio needs guest drivers (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows); sata and scsi work without them.

thin.description: true creates a sparse qcow2 that grows on use; false preallocates the full size.

boot_order.description: 0 keeps the disk out of the boot order. Non-zero values are unique across every disk and boot.media_boot_order and number the boot devices from 1 with no gaps.

VMDisk.description: One virtual disk, created inside the VM's own exclusive directory on its storage target. Disks are never shared or reused: Core checks exclusive ownership for every disk and free space per storage target, summing the disks that land on the same target.

mode.description: dedicated preallocates and locks the ceiling in host RAM while running: memory and currentMemory at size_mib, no balloon, and memoryBacking with immediate allocation, locked and nosharepages. Stopped VMs release physical RAM but retain their Nex capacity commitment. QEMU overhead is locked too. Requires updated Core; existing VMs need full shutdown, a successful stopped vm-update save and start. Legacy dedicated live edits fail before device effects with a stop-and-save instruction. Upgrade, autostart or guest reboot alone does not rewrite old definitions. maximum caps without reserving: the same ceiling plus a virtio balloon with free page reporting, so the guest returns pages it frees. Reclaim requires the balloon driver running in the guest (built into Linux; virtio-win guest tools on Windows); without it the guest drifts to the ceiling and holds it. There is no pressure-driven reclaim daemon.

size_mib.description: Memory ceiling in MiB. Both sides require at least 512; Controller caps the request at 262144.

VMMemory.description: Memory ceiling and how the host treats it. size_mib is the ceiling in both modes and host capacity preflight uses that ceiling in both modes: a VM that cannot reach its ceiling is refused. dedicated additionally counts against committed capacity; maximum reserves nothing and is allowed to oversubscribe.

network_id.description: Registered network that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool, resolved by resource ID.

model.description: Which network card the guest sees. virtio is paravirtualised: fastest and lowest host CPU, but the guest needs a driver (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows). e1000 and e1000e emulate Intel gigabit cards nearly every OS already drives, for guests and installers that cannot see a virtio adapter, at higher host CPU. rtl8139 emulates a 100 Mbit card for guests too old for a gigabit driver; the limit is the emulated hardware. vmxnet3 is VMware's paravirtualised adapter, for guests already carrying VMware drivers.

mac.description: Empty derives a stable MAC from the VM ID and the interface index (protocol.DerivedMAC: the 52:54:00 locally administered prefix, two octets of sha256(id) and the index), which never collides across a VM's at most 8 interfaces. A manual address must be six octets in canonical lower-case colon form and unicast; the pattern encodes the cleared multicast bit as an even second hex digit. All-zero addresses are refused, addresses are unique within the VM, and Controller additionally enforces uniqueness across the pool by plain string comparison. The VM list reports the effective address, and an edit freezes every automatic address into the definition (drawn from the VM's derived range above the highest index the VM uses, or the lowest free index when none above is free), so interfaces keep their identity across later edits.

mtu.description: Interface MTU, or 0 for the network's own. Accepted only when model is virtio: QEMU communicates an MTU to the guest through virtio's host_mtu feature and libvirt sizes the host tap to match, while the emulated models have no equivalent and would leave the guest on its own default. A value on any other model is refused rather than silently applied to the host side only. The floor is the IPv6 minimum MTU and the ceiling the largest jumbo frame common NICs accept; every device along the path must agree or traffic is dropped without an error.

VMNIC.description: One virtual network interface on a registered pool network. A VM may have none and at most 8.

VMUpdateEvidence.description: Untagged Go struct: JSON members use Go field names.

mount_path.description: Original existing ZFS dataset mount path. It rejects Unicode whitespace/control characters, percent and backslash because Core uses it as a systemd What value.

CPUFeature.description: Native CPU feature policy. Names must be unique within one CPU definition; no guest-OS feature policy is inferred.

features.description: Optional fixed native CPU feature list. Omitted or empty retains model-only behavior. Nonempty requires a named model (not host modes or max) and vm-cpu-baseline-v1. Duplicate feature names are rejected.

CPUBaseline.description: Disposable Core-master observation for every current non-ejected ready pool member, including a single-host pool. Native baseline and exact destination comparisons must succeed under unchanged membership. Errors or absent observations are unavailable, never an inferred smaller pool. Saved VM definitions are independent; future members and live migration are not certified.

cpu.description: Native guest CPU XML derived from libvirt host-model capabilities, including feature overrides.

features.description: Optional fixed native CPU feature list. Omitted or empty retains model-only behavior. Nonempty requires a named model (not host modes or max) and vm-cpu-baseline-v1. Duplicate feature names are rejected.

source.description: Bridge name used by guest interfaces (derived <uplink>v<vlan> for kind vlan) or libvirt network name.

uplink.description: Uplink NIC name: required for kind vlan; set on kind bridge when the registration was created automatically for the untagged network of a bridge on a physical port.

generation.description: kind vlan: master-owned desired generation members reconcile against; 0 on host-local registrations.

member_access.description: kind vlan: the master's observations of each member's applied bridge; absent on host-local registrations.

tombstone.description: The host durably removed this network. The row carries only id, pool_id, host_id and the generation after the removal; name, kind, source and the rest are absent. A Controller deletes its mirror row for that host and never re-adopts the registration from an older report, and a peer list never carries one.

NetworkRegistration.description: Pool guest network on one host: an existing bridge, an active libvirt network, or a Core-created VLAN bridge (kind vlan) on an uplink NIC. VLAN bridges are additive; the management bridge, addresses and routes are never changed. The host self-registers the untagged default network of every host bridge on a physical NIC or bond (<port> untagged, kind bridge, uplink recorded) in its own journal with host-generated IDs, at agent start and when a new uplink appears; Controller creates registrations itself only by adoption (actor system): any network the host reports in Inventory.managed.networks that Controller does not hold (request_id adopt-network:<host>:<id>, ID and name preserved). A bridge or libvirt network already held by another registration on that host is a failed host result, not an HTTP 409.

size_bytes.description: Zero until a URL download completes; applied media is at least 32774 bytes.

url.description: Command-only public HTTP(S) source URL. Omitted from client responses and applied host inventory. Requires iso-download-v1.

generation.description: Fences removal, as it does for storage and networks. Imports leave it zero and every reader treats zero as 1.

tombstone.description: The host durably removed this ISO and unlinked its published file. The row carries only id, pool_id, host_id and the generation after the removal; a Controller deletes its mirror row for that host and never re-adopts the import from an older report.

PoolWrappedKey.description: The pool CA private key sealed for exactly one member of one generation: ECDH between a fresh ephemeral P-256 key and that member's certified peer public key, HKDF-SHA256 with a context binding pool ID, member host ID and generation, then AES-256-GCM with the same context as additional data. A member stores it sealed and never opens it while it is a member; nothing in this release unwraps it. All three fields are standard base64.

ephemeral_public_key.description: Base64 uncompressed P-256 point of the master's per-push ephemeral key.

nonce.description: Base64 12-byte AES-GCM nonce, fresh for every push.

ciphertext.description: Base64 AES-256-GCM ciphertext of the pool CA private key PEM.

PoolReplicaSection.description: One declared section of an authority replica and the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON. A member recomputes every digest and refuses a replica that declares a different set, so a section cannot be dropped, reordered or replaced.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of that section's canonical JSON.

PoolAuthorityReplica.description: The pool master's signed, read-only copy of its own durable pool authority, pushed to one member. It is stored by every ready member and acted on by none of them: no membership, VM, storage, network or media record on the receiving host is read from or changed by a replica, and no health judgement is derived from one. The signature is made with the pool CA key over every field but signature, so a member verifies it against the pool CA it pinned at join, long after the master that signed it is gone. Bounded to 1 MiB on the wire and on disk.

generation.description: The master's authority generation, which it advances only when the replicated content digest changes. Never 0 in a valid replica; generations may skip.

member_host_id.description: The one member this copy is addressed to. It is inside the signature, so a replica cannot be re-addressed in transit and a copy wrapped for one member cannot be presented to another.

vms.description: The master's pool-vms.json owner projection, replicated as received bytes so ownership, epochs, specs and pending updates survive unchanged. Published per-host inventory snapshots are deliberately not replicated: they are observations, and a promoted master re-collects fresh ones.

storage.description: Pool storage registrations with credential receipts stripped, exactly as the storage peer list strips them.

fence_credentials.description: The pool's fence credential material, sealed for this member alone. Like ca_key_wrapped it is covered by signature and excluded from the content digest, so one generation still has one digest for every member; what makes new material advance the generation is fence_credential_version in the membership.

sections.description: Exactly the six sections above, in order.

signature.description: Base64 ASN.1 ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 signature by the pool CA key over the whole replica with signature empty.

PoolReplicaAck.description: The member's answer to one push. Re-pushing the same generation with the same content returns the same acknowledgement; a refusal carries a bounded reason and a 409, never a silent drop.

host_id.description: The acknowledging member. Empty in a refusal that could not be attributed.

digest.description: Content digest of the stored replica: identical on every member of one generation, because the per-member address, the per-push wrap, the creation time, the signature and the generation are excluded from it.

verified.description: True only when the replica was verified against the pool CA, its sections recomputed, and the file durably written.

error.description: Bounded refusal reason; control characters collapse the whole message to "pool authority replica refused".

PoolReplicaStatus.description: Observed replica state, reported in a member's inventory.managed.replica and returned by the peer GET. It is what a host holds and how fresh that observation is; the Controller mirrors it for display and stores none of it.

generation.description: 0 when this host holds no replica.

received_at.description: When this host stored it, from the host's own clock, so freshness survives a restart.

error.description: The last refusal this host recorded, kept alongside whatever it still holds; a later accepted push clears it.

operation_id.description: The Controller operation that started the transfer, or the identifier the transfer was recorded under.

action.description: promote or eject: Core's own name for what this transfer does. A fence-verified promotion of a surviving member is also promote, and is told apart by role: candidate. The Controller's requested action (master-change, eject, transfer-cancel) is reported separately in last_transfer.

role.description: This host's part in the transfer: source is the pool master that started it, target is the host taking the authority, ejected is the host leaving the pool, candidate is the surviving member running a fence-verified promotion.

target_host_id.description: The transfer's subject: the host becoming master, or the host being ejected.

stage.description: The stage this host has durably reached. For a master change: freeze, replicate, activate (the signed hand-off), repoint (every other host is told, in the new master's own signed words, who the master is now). For an eject: freeze, remove (the durable membership change, after which nothing stays frozen), repoint, leave. For a promotion: preflight, fence, activate, repoint. done and aborted are terminal.

status.description: pending while the hosts are still running it; needs_attention means durable and still running, not an error.

error.description: This host's own last refusal or failure, bounded and sanitized.

authority_generation.description: The pool authority generation this transfer is pinned to.

frozen.description: True while this host is refusing pool authority writes for the transfer. Running guests are unaffected and stop is never refused.

cancellable.description: Core's own answer to "may this still be cancelled?", so no caller has to infer it from stage names. True only before the transfer's first irreversible durable step: a master change until the pool-CA-signed hand-off, an eject until the membership without that member is written, and never for a promotion, which fences. It is computed from the same predicate the cancel itself is gated on, so the reported flag and the accepted cancel cannot drift. It is always present: a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer and never has to tell "not cancellable" from "not reported".

handed_off.description: The outgoing master's own durable answer to "have I signed this pool's authority away?", reported rather than inferred from stage names or refusal sentences. Only the source records it, so a target or ejected host always reports false. It is always present, so an older Core that omits it is distinguishable from one that reports false.

observed_at.description: When this host wrote this report.

PoolTransferStatus.description: One participant's own report of the master change or eject it is part of. Every participant reports its own; nothing merges them into a job, and a host that is not reporting says nothing rather than repeating its last stage.

generation.description: The pool master's own durable authority generation. This is the only absolute generation in the pool; nothing else derives one.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the authority content that generation numbered.

PoolAuthorityRecord.description: Reported by the pool master alone. A Controller mirrors it to compare each member's acknowledged replica generation against it and stores neither.

from_host_id.description: The host that issued and signed this notice.

target_host_id.description: The transfer's subject: the promoted host, or the ejected one.

authority_generation.description: The exact authority generation being handed over, or the generation the issuing master holds.

signature.description: Base64 ASN.1 ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 over the whole notice minus this field, made with the pool CA key. Every recipient verifies it against the pool CA it pinned at join, so no host takes another host's word for who the master is.

PoolAuthorityNotice.description: The pool-CA-signed statement that pool authority moved. Used twice in one transfer: the hand-off, signed by the outgoing master, naming the exact generation it froze and the host it handed that generation to (membership empty); and the re-point, signed by the new master with the pool CA key it now holds, carrying the new membership at a strictly higher membership generation. A notice without a signature, or at a generation that is not strictly higher, is refused.

operation_id.description: Idempotency key: the same request repeated after a lost reply returns the same answer and performs the step at most once.

action.description: activate hands the authority to the addressed host; abort records that it never activated and never will for this operation; repoint moves the addressed host onto the new master; leave tells an ejected host it has left.

PoolTransferRequest.description: One step of a transfer, addressed to one peer. abort carries no meaningful notice; every other action requires one whose operation_id matches.

activated.description: The fact an abort needs: whether this host had already adopted the authority, decided once under its own lock, so an abort and an activation can never both succeed.

authority_generation.description: This host's authority generation after the step.

membership_generation.description: This host's membership generation after the step.

notice.description: Returned with an accepted activation: the new master's own signed re-point notice, so the outgoing master demotes itself on signed evidence rather than on its assumption that the activation worked.

PoolTransferReply.description: The addressed host's own answer to one transfer step.

host_id.description: The host that answered the probe.

role.description: This host's own role in the pool it names.

master_host_id.description: The host this host currently follows as pool master.

master_peer_origin.description: That master's peer origin, so a converging host can go on to probe it.

authority_generation.description: This host's own pool authority generation; 0 on a member.

membership_generation.description: The membership generation this host holds.

replica_generation.description: The generation of the authority replica this host stores.

replica_verified.description: Whether that replica was proven against the pool CA.

frozen.description: This host is refusing pool authority writes for a transfer.

handed_off.description: This host has signed its authority away and refuses every authority write for good, not only while frozen.

caller_status.description: The membership status this host holds for the calling certificate, decided from the certificate the transport proved rather than from a name in a body. Empty when it names no member at all. This is how an ejected host learns it has been ejected.

transfer.description: This host's own part of a transfer.

notice.description: A master answers a ready member that is behind with a signed re-point notice, so a host that missed a push converges from whichever host it can reach without having to trust a stale one. The probe answer alone changes nothing; only the signature at a strictly higher generation does.

restricted.description: This host's own refusal to act on pool authority, set while it cannot prove it holds the pool's current authority. A returning fenced master answers its probes with this, which is how a member and an operator see that it came back and is refusing to start anything.

vms.description: This host's own view of the VM definitions it owns, answered only when the caller asks with ?vms=1. Consumed by the promotion proof of a later slice.

vms_reported.description: Separates "this host defines no VM" from "this host could not read its own record": an empty vms list means the first only when this is true.

PoolAuthorityStatus.description: The read-only authority probe every host answers to any holder of a certificate this pool's CA issued, including one this pool has ejected. It is how a returning or restarted host discovers that it has been superseded or ejected, and how a host that missed a re-point finds the current master without trusting a stale one.

host_id.description: The host that defines this VM, as that host itself reports it.

revision.description: The definition revision this host holds.

PoolVMOwnership.description: One host's own statement about one VM it defines, answered by the authority probe only when the caller asks for it. The execution epoch is deliberately absent: it is the master's number and a member could only repeat it back rather than confirm it. Consumed by the promotion proof of a later slice, which is not documented in this release.

kind.description: The structural form of reason, so no caller has to match on the sentence. unconfirmed is a master that has not re-proved its authority since it restarted; superseded is a host that found a higher authority elsewhere. Omitted by an older Core, in which case the sentence is the only signal.

reason.description: Why this host is refusing to act on pool authority.

conflicts.description: VMs this host still defines that the current pool master records as running elsewhere. A conflict is never resolved by guessing.

PoolRestrictedStatus.description: A Core-enforced refusal state on a host that cannot prove it holds the pool's current authority: while it is set the host writes no pool authority, mints no authority generation, starts no workload and autostarts nothing. Stop, power-off, console, local recovery access and reporting are untouched, and the libvirt hook refuses managed shared-VM starts by reading the host's own durable record, so the refusal holds with no Controller connected. It is reported by the authority probe, by inventory.managed.restricted and by GET /api/local/v1/pool.

credential_ref.description: Core's own opaque reference for the material. It names a file in the host's state directory and is never projected to a client.

version.description: The master's counter for the material, so a member can tell a re-wrap of the same material from new material. It is mirrored in PoolMember.fence_credential_version, which is what makes rotated material advance the pool authority generation.

wrapped.description: The material sealed for this member alone, by the same primitive and with the same guarantees as the pool CA key, under its own context binding pool, member, generation, fenced host and reference.

PoolWrappedFenceCredential.description: One host's fence credential material carried to one member inside that member's replica. The host that actually fences during a promotion is a surviving member, and it cannot be given the material after the master it must fence is gone, so the material travels sealed rather than not at all. A member stores it sealed in its 0600 replica and opens it only while it performs a promotion; the Controller never sees it, and it never reaches SQLite, the audit trail, a response or a log. Every ready member can open the material addressed to it, which is the same trust model the sealed pool CA key already carries: admit only hosts you trust with powering off a profiled host.

name.description: replica-integrity: this host holds a verified signed replica. replica-supremacy: no reachable host holds a newer pool authority. accepted-ownership: every pool VM is recorded the same way by the host that owns it. old-master-exclusion: the old pool master has been fenced and its power-off observed by Core itself.

status.description: unknown blocks a promotion exactly as blocked does. It is a different word only so an operator can tell a refusal from an outage, and it is never presented as "fine". old-master-exclusion is normally unknown before the promotion runs, because Core fences and proves it during the promotion and never during a preflight.

hosts.description: The hosts this check is about.

vms.description: The pool VMs this check is about.

PoolPromotionCheck.description: One named check of the promotion proof, computed on the candidate from its own replica and its own live probes.

reachable.description: Whether the candidate reached this host over the pool network. An unreachable host is reported unreachable, never assumed stopped.

role.description: master or member, as that host answered.

authority_generation.description: The pool authority generation that host answered with.

replica_generation.description: The replica generation that host holds.

membership_generation.description: The membership generation that host holds.

blocks.description: This host's own answer to "does this host stop the promotion as things stand": an unreachable member that could itself have been promoted, or a reachable one that disagrees. A blocking host that can be fenced appears in the verdict's fence_host_ids; one that cannot is a refusal an operator must resolve another way.

fence_recorded.description: Whether a fence profile is recorded for this host at all.

fence_usable.description: Whether the candidate could turn that profile into a proof for this host: a profile kind this build can verify, plus a credential sealed to the candidate that it can open.

fence_unusable_reason.description: Core's own short sentence when it could not.

fence_kind.description: The recorded fence profile's kind, so a caller can show which method this promotion would shut this host out with. Empty when no profile is recorded.

fence_check_warning.description: Advisory only: what this candidate's own last non-destructive check of that fence device found, when it was failing or stale. The promotion's proof path is unchanged and still decides; this exists so an operator is not surprised by a fence device that was already known to be unreachable.

error.description: The probe's own bounded failure text.

PoolPromotionHost.description: One probed host of the replica's membership, as the promotion candidate found it, with that host's own contribution to the verdict: whether it blocks the promotion, and whether the candidate could exclude it by a fence if it does.

host_id.description: The host the pool authority records as this VM's owner.

state.description: confirmed by its reachable owner, fenced with its owner, or blocked. A blocked VM does not block the pool's promotion; it stays visible and unstartable until it is reconciled, and its definition is never deleted.

reason.description: Core's own sentence for a blocked VM.

PoolPromotionVM.description: One VM record of the replica, classified by the candidate against what the owning host itself reports.

candidate_host_id.description: The surviving member this verdict is about: the host that would become master.

old_master_host_id.description: The pool master this promotion would exclude.

operation_id.description: The promotion this verdict was computed for, when it belongs to one.

authority_generation.description: The generation the candidate would promote from.

can_promote.description: True only when the whole proof holds right now, fence included. In the normal ready state it is false, because the old master has not been fenced yet: that is an honest "not proved", not a refusal. A caller must not use it alone to decide whether to offer the promotion.

ready_to_fence.description: The state a caller offers the operator the promotion in: every check but the exclusion has passed, the exclusion is unknown only because no fence has been attempted, and the candidate holds a usable fence profile and an openable credential for every host in fence_host_ids. Confirming now proceeds to the fence rather than to a refusal.

fence_required.description: Whether this promotion needs a fence proof at all.

fence_recorded.description: Whether the old pool master has a fence profile recorded in the membership at all.

fence_usable.description: Whether this host could turn that profile into a proof: a profile kind this build can verify, plus a credential sealed to this host that it can open. Only virsh profiles can be recorded by this build, so a physical pool reports false.

fence_unusable_reason.description: Core's own short single-line sentence when it could not: "no fence profile is recorded for <host>", "this host holds no fence credential for <host>", or vmhost.PoolFenceUsable's own sentence such as "this host does not report a unique hardware identity, so a management controller cannot be confirmed to be its own".

fence_host_ids.description: Every host this promotion would power off, sorted: the old pool master, and every other host that blocks the promotion and can be excluded by a fence. It is what the operator confirms and what the promotion command carries back verbatim, so a host is never powered off without having been named to the operator first.

checks.description: Every named check, in Core's order.

hosts.description: Every host of the replica's membership, as the candidate probed it.

vms.description: Every pool VM of the replica, classified.

fence.description: The fence proof Core produced, when one exists. Always absent from a preflight: a preflight fences nothing.

blocking.description: Every blocking sentence, so a caller can show what must change without matching on check names. can_promote is exactly "this list is empty".

observed_at.description: When the candidate computed this verdict. A verdict is an observation with a lifetime, not a record: it is recomputed, never stored.

PoolPromotionVerdict.description: The promotion candidate Core's whole structured answer, computed on Core from its own signed replica and its own live probes of the pool network. A preflight returns it without changing anything, so an operator sees exactly what blocks before confirming a destructive fence. Nothing in it is computed, cached or stored by the Controller.

stage.description: The stage the candidate has durably reached: preflight, fence, activate, repoint, done or aborted.

status.description: needs_attention means durable and still running on Core, not an error.

error.description: The candidate's own last refusal or failure, bounded and sanitized.

verdict.description: The last verdict this host computed for the promotion.

cancellable.description: Core's own answer to "may this still be cancelled?". A promotion fences the old master, so it is never true; it is reported rather than inferred so a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer. It is always present: a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer and never has to tell "not cancellable" from "not reported".

observed_at.description: When this host wrote this report.

PoolPromotionStatus.description: The promotion candidate's own report of the fence-verified promotion it is running. Reported as inventory.managed.promotion; the Controller stores no stage, no candidate and no verdict.

membership.description: The full membership record for the pool actions that carry one. For join and maintenance only master_host_id is set: the master reads its own record, and a membership composed in the Controller could already be stale.

expected_version.description: The membership generation the operator saw. 0 or absent means unchecked. For action maintenance it is compared against the master's own current membership generation, not against the membership on the wire.

member_host_id.description: For action join, the joining host: it is the command's target, and the pool-join command is the one pool command not delivered to the master. For action maintenance it names the host being drained, which is not the target: that command goes to the master, addressed by membership.master_host_id.

enabled.description: For action maintenance, the desired drain state of member_host_id. It is a desired state, not a transition: re-sending the state the host is already in succeeds and leaves maintenance_since unmoved.

master_url.description: Bare HTTPS origin of the master's pool-peer listener that the joining Core dials. Required for action join.

pool_ca_pem.description: Master's pool CA, pinned by the joining Core for the peer exchange. Required for action join. Never returned by any Controller read route.

invitation.description: Single-use, 15-minute, pool- and host-bound join credential issued by the master and redeemed by the joining Core itself. Required for action join. The Controller relays it and never returns, lists, logs or audits it; the stored command row is scrubbed of this field and pool_ca_pem as soon as the operation leaves queued, and unconditionally 15 minutes after issue.

peer_origin.description: Optional bare HTTPS origin the joining host advertises to its new master after it is admitted.

fence.description: The power-fence profile to record for member_host_id, on action fence-profile. null clears the recorded profile. Any credential the operator supplied has already been delivered to Core over the one-time encrypted credential handoff before this command is written, and only the opaque reference Core allocated appears here.
